**Running many agents no longer freezes the host: new agents get a memory ceiling of 8 GiB, at most half the host, and stay out of its swap, and "Never freeze my CPU" keeps a core or more free for your desktop however many agents run. A new agent shows as Initializing while it's being made, instead of Needs attention.**

## What's new

- **Never freeze my CPU.** A new setting in **Settings → Every agent**: a switch, and how many
  cores to keep free, 1 by default. While it's on, the CPU limits of all running agents add up to
  at most the host's cores minus those, recomputed whenever an agent is made, started, stopped,
  paused, resumed or destroyed. Agents keep their own limits when they fit; when they don't, the
  cores are shared as evenly as possible, never below one each. The limit changes live, without
  restarting anything. What you chose for an agent is kept, and put back when there's room again
  or the setting is turned off. The agent's Overview shows when it's held below its own limit
  ("held to N cores"), and so do `agentbox limits` and `agentbox top`; `agentbox limits` with no
  agent shows or changes the setting.
- **New agents get a memory limit.** 8 GiB, or half the host's memory if that's less, on new
  installations and on existing ones that never set one. A size you chose is kept, and so is
  "no limit" once you choose it. Change it in **Settings → Resources for new agents**, or per agent.
- **Capped agents stay out of swap.** An agent with a memory limit can't push its pages into the
  host's swap, which on a zram host is compressed RAM paid for with the desktop's CPU. An agent past
  its ceiling is stopped by the kernel inside its own machine: its build fails and says so, and the
  host keeps working. Agents with no limit swap as before. Existing agents get this the next time
  their limits are edited.
- **Initializing.** A new agent shows **Initializing** while it's being made, instead of
  **Needs attention** in red. **Needs attention** is left for a create that failed or was
  interrupted.

## Fixes

- **Opus and Sonnet offer the 1M context window again.** 0.3.0 still offered only 200k for them in
  Settings and `create_agent` on installations where a chat had run without a compact window set.
  The wrong 200k is dropped once, on upgrade.
- **The Arch package installs on current Arch.** 0.3.0's `.pacman` depended on `http-parser`,
  which Arch no longer ships, so `pacman -U` refused it.

## What went wrong

- **The 1M window.** 0.3.0 stopped taking a session's compact window for its model's window, but
  not when no compact window was set: Claude Code then compacts at its own default of 200k and
  reports that, and AgentBox kept it. That case now counts as 200k too.
- **The Arch package.** electron-builder's default dependency list for `.pacman` still names
  `http-parser`. The package now declares its own list, without it.

## Install

```bash
chmod +x AgentBox-0.4.0-x86_64.AppImage
./AgentBox-0.4.0-x86_64.AppImage
```

Or, on Debian/Ubuntu, `sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.4.0-amd64.deb`; on Arch, `sudo pacman -U
AgentBox-0.4.0-x64.pacman`. On a Mac, open the `.dmg` and drag AgentBox into Applications. On
Windows, run the installer or the portable `.exe`. See the README's
[Install](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/blob/v0.4.0/README.md#install) for the rest.

**Upgrading from 0.3.0:** the base image is unchanged, so there's nothing to rebuild.

## Known limitations

- **A memory ceiling can fail a build** that needs more than it: an agent past its limit is
  stopped by the kernel rather than slowed down by swap. Raise the agent's limit, even while it
  runs.
- **Never freeze my CPU** shares whole cores; it doesn't use `limits.cpu.allowance`.
- The rest are unchanged since
  [0.3.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.3.0),
  [0.2.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.2.0) and
  [0.1.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.1.0).
